headline: UNOOSA convened a Vienna consultation on space transparency under the Outer Space Treaty, as OpenAI fired three safety researchers who then published an open letter, and the UK AI Security Institute announced new measures against AI risks.

points.text: The UN Office for Outer Space Affairs convened a Vienna consultation on information-sharing related to space activities and implementation of Article XI of the Outer Space Treaty, aimed at building trust through greater transparency.
OpenAI fired three safety researchers, Tomek Korbak, Mikita Balesni and Jasmine Wang, ostensibly for mishandling sensitive company information; the researchers have published an open letter.
The UK AI Security Institute announced a suite of measures meant to better protect Britain from the risks posed by increasingly powerful AI.
The US Army created a new robotics technician role to advise commanders on deploying autonomous systems during operations, building expertise in drone warfare.
A commentary warned that states must set limits on emergency powers before an AI crisis is used to justify lasting executive control.
A newsletter examined the 'center-satellite' structure behind American data center hegemony.
Microsoft unveiled its third-generation Maia AI chip, aiming to reduce its reliance on Nvidia GPUs for AI inference.
